For **one typical electric blanket**, I’d get a **1,000Wh-class power station**. The [BLUETTI Elite 100 V2](https://www.blackoutwise.com/best/best-power-station-for-electric-blanket) is a good fit: it has a 1,024Wh battery, and one estimate puts runtime at about 12 hours for a 150W blanket that cycles on and off.

As a conservative guide, a blanket averaging around 100W could use nearly the whole usable capacity of a 1kWh station over an 8-hour night. If your blanket runs hotter, draws more, or you want extra margin, consider a roughly 2kWh unit. Check the blanket’s wattage label before buying; small 300Wh stations generally won’t last all night. ([Runtime estimates and sizing](https://homepowerfacts.com/can-it-run/electric-blanket/))

Another 1,024Wh option is the [EcoFlow Delta 3 Classic](https://www.techradar.com/pro/this-ecoflow-delta-3-classic-bundle-is-the-home-backup-battery-id-keep-ready-for-winter-storms-and-its-usd119-off-at-best-buy), which has ample AC output for a blanket. Plug the blanket directly into the station, and keep the station off the bed and away from the blanket. ([Use guidance](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-run-a-heated-blanket-all-night))
